title: Favorite banjo and guitar players
summary: Banjoists he admired and Johnny St. Cyr and Rene Hall on guitar.

blocks.x: He painted in there. Some of your favorite, say, banjo players when you started banjo.

Well, when I first started Kimball. Kimball was all over the country, you know, the first time I heard Kimball, another fellow from Donaldsonville by the name of Clarence Ellis. Never heard of him? Never. He used to call himself Duke Ellis. He played in the deluxe band in Baton Rouge. Duke Ellis? Mm-hmm.
I heard so many guys, you know, you can't remember them all. What about guitar, when you started on guitar? Did you have anybody you liked?

Well, I always liked Johnny Sincere. Home of Eugene, Rennie Hall. Rennie Hall was my favorite. Because he was a modern of that time, you know. And then come home of Eugene and then, well I fancy Johnny. Johnny was traditional for, he always played the guitar with the bass line.

And I liked that. That's what caused me to play the bass now, you know. Yeah. I listen to Johnny Sincere. The electric bass. Yeah, electric bass. I used to go back to his house on the Edmburg Street when he was living back then.
You know, he always did pick that one. Yeah, his bass line. He'd pick a bass line and chords.
He'd carry the bass line with him all the time. Oh yeah.
That was nice. I thought the way he played.
Yeah, I liked it. I liked the way he played. When I first met Johnny Sincere, he was living on Ramport and Pedita, upstairs. I didn't take a lesson from him. You didn't know him, huh?
No, I didn't know he ever lived there.
Ramport and Pedita. And then later on he bought a home back on the Edmburg Street.
